stories.headline: US Forces Open Hormuz Lane, Sink 6 Iranian Boats; UAE Hit by Missiles for First Time Since Ceasefire

key_facts.fact: US military fired on Iranian forces and sank six small boats targeting civilian ships as it moved to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Monday May 4
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. military said it fired on Iranian forces and sank six small boats targeting civilian ships as it moved to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Monday.

key_facts.fact: Two American-flagged merchant ships successfully transited the strait on Monday under a new US-led initiative
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. military said two American-flagged merchant ships had successfully transited the strait on Monday as part of a new initiative.

key_facts.fact: UAE air defenses engaged 15 missiles and 4 drones fired by Iran; a drone struck a Fujairah oil facility, wounding three Indian nationals
key_facts.excerpt: The UAE Defense Ministry said its air defenses had engaged 15 missiles and four drones fired by Iran. Authorities in the eastern emirate of Fujairah said one drone sparked a fire at a key oil facility, wounding three Indian nationals.

key_facts.fact: Adm. Brad Cooper said US forces opened a passage through the strait free of Iranian mines and defeated 'each and every' threat launched at civilian ships
key_facts.excerpt: Adm. Brad Cooper, commander of U.S. Central Command, told reporters that American forces have successfully opened a passage through the strait that is free of Iranian mines.

key_facts.fact: Iran's foreign minister warned both the US and UAE 'should be wary of being dragged back into quagmire'; Iran called the incident a result of 'US military adventurism'
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on X that both the U.S. and the UAE 'should be wary of being dragged back into quagmire.'

key_facts.fact: US and Gulf Arab nations are drafting a new UN Security Council resolution to condemn Iran for blocking the strait, co-drafted by US and Bahrain with Saudi, Qatar, UAE and Kuwait input
key_facts.excerpt: The United States and Gulf Arab nations are drafting a U.N. Security Council resolution designed to condemn Iran for blocking the Strait of Hormuz... The U.S. is co-drafting the new resolution with Bahrain with input from Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia.

key_facts.fact: Iran's latest ceasefire proposal calls for US lifting sanctions, ending the blockade, withdrawing forces from the region, and ceasing all hostilities including Israel's operations in Lebanon
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's latest proposal for ending the war calls for the U.S. lifting sanctions, ending the blockade, withdrawing forces from the region and ceasing all hostilities, including Israel's operations in Lebanon.

sources.title: U.S. tries to open Hormuz Strait as UAE says Iran attacked it
US, Gulf Arab nations draft new UN resolution on Strait of Hormuz

stories.headline: US Confirms 25% Tariff on EU Cars, Breaking Trade Deal; EU Finance Ministers Warn of Retaliation

key_facts.fact: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told EU and German trade officials the US will move forward with raising EU car tariffs to 25% from the agreed 15%
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told European Union and German trade officials over the weekend that the U.S. will move forward with President Donald Trump's plan to raise EU car import tariffs to 25%.

key_facts.fact: Trump announced the tariff hike on Friday May 1, claiming the EU had not complied with their trade deal reached in August 2025 at Turnberry
key_facts.excerpt: Trump said on Friday he would increase tariffs on cars and trucks from the European Union to 25% next week from the previously agreed 15%, saying the bloc had not complied with its trade deal with Washington.

key_facts.fact: European Commission rejected Trump's claim of non-compliance, arguing the EU is still going through its legislative process to ratify the deal
key_facts.excerpt: The European Commission rejected Trump's claim that Brussels was not complying with last summer's trade deal and said it would keep its options open to protect EU interests if Washington breached the terms of the agreement.

key_facts.fact: EU finance ministers said all retaliatory options are on the table; German Vice-Chancellor Lars Klingbeil said 'we would be prepared if an escalation were to occur'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Our path is clear, we don't want an escalation, we want a joint solution with the Americans,' said German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil, who is also vice-chancellor. However, he added, 'we would be prepared if an escalation were to occur.'

key_facts.fact: The tariff hike came amid US-EU tensions over the Iran war; the White House also announced plans to remove 5,000 US troops from Germany
key_facts.excerpt: Trump fired off the tariff post amid escalating tensions between the U.S. and the EU over the war in Iran and European countries' refusal to send navies to open the Strait of Hormuz. The White House said Friday it plans to remove 5,000 U.S. troops from Germany.

key_facts.fact: Shares in Porsche, BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen all fell 2-3% on Monday; the pan-European automobiles index dropped 2.3%
key_facts.excerpt: The pan-European automobiles and parts index was down 2.3% as of 1046 GMT, while shares in Porsche, BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen were all down 2% to 3%.

sources.title: US to move forward with plans to hike EU car tariffs
EU Vows Action If Trump Adopts Car Tariffs, But Urges Restraint

stories.headline: China Invokes Anti-Sanctions Law for First Time, Orders Companies to Defy US Blacklist on Oil Refiners

key_facts.fact: China's Ministry of Commerce on May 2 ordered companies not to comply with US sanctions against five refiners, the first time Beijing has used its 2021 blocking rules
key_facts.excerpt: On Saturday (May 2), the Ministry of Commerce ordered companies not to comply with US sanctions against five refiners, including the recently designated Hengli Petrochemical, citing a law that allows Beijing to retaliate against entities enforcing sanctions it deems unlawful.

key_facts.fact: The five sanctioned refiners include Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian), Shandong Jincheng, Hebei Xinhai Chemical, Shandong Shengxing Chemical, and Shandong Shouguang Luqing
key_facts.excerpt: The five US-sanctioned Chinese oil refiners: Shandong Shouguang Luqing Petrochemical Co Ltd, Shandong Shengxing Chemical Co Ltd, Hebei Xinhai Chemical Group Co Ltd, Shandong Jincheng Petrochemical Group Co Ltd, Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian) Refinery Co Ltd.

key_facts.fact: Under the law (revised April 2026), China can impose countermeasures on companies and individuals including trade, investment curbs and entry/exit restrictions
key_facts.excerpt: Under the law, introduced in 2021 and most recently revised in April, China can impose countermeasures on companies and individuals, including trade and investment curbs and entry and exit restrictions.

key_facts.fact: The move comes less than two weeks before Trump is due to visit Beijing on May 14-15 for a summit with Xi Jinping
key_facts.excerpt: The unprecedented move sets the stage for a potential showdown just days before President Donald Trump's highly anticipated state visit to Beijing.

key_facts.fact: A White House official warned: 'Any company considering skirting US sanctions should think twice'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Any company considering skirting US sanctions should think twice,' a White House official told Reuters without elaborating on the Chinese order.

key_facts.fact: Independent 'teapot' refiners in China are the main buyers of Iran's oil exports; Iran accounts for roughly 13% of China's oil imports and China for 90%+ of Iran's crude exports
key_facts.excerpt: Iran is a major source of China's oil imports, accounting for roughly 13 percent, according to estimates by shipping analytics firm Kpler. China is believed to account for more than 90 percent of Iran's crude exports.

sources.title: China invokes rules to blunt US sanctions on 'teapot' refiners
China uses anti-sanctions law to counter US blacklisting of refiners that bought Iranian crude

stories.headline: Global Chip Sales Hit $298.5B in Q1 2026, Up 25% QoQ; Industry On Track for $1 Trillion Year

key_facts.fact: Global semiconductor sales were $298.5 billion in Q1 2026, up 25% from Q4 2025; March sales were $99.5 billion, up 79.2% year-over-year
key_facts.excerpt: Global semiconductor sales were $298.5 billion during the first quarter of 2026, an increase of 25% compared to Q4 of 2025. Global sales were $99.5 billion during the month of March 2026, an increase of 79.2% compared to the March 2025 total of $55.5 billion.

key_facts.fact: SIA president John Neuffer said global chip sales 'remain on track to reach $1 trillion in 2026'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Global chip sales remain on track to reach $1 trillion in 2026, with Q1 sales significantly exceeding sales in Q4 2025,' said John Neuffer, SIA president and CEO.

key_facts.fact: Asia Pacific/All Other region led with 108.5% year-over-year growth in March, followed by Americas at 83.1% and China at 74.8%
key_facts.excerpt: Regionally, year-to-year sales in March were up in the Asia Pacific/All Other (108.5%), the Americas (83.1%), China (74.8%), Europe (46.5%), and Japan (7.4%).

key_facts.fact: SEMI chief Ajit Manocha told Reuters that geopolitical risks are unlikely to curtail the semiconductor boom this year, though material shortages may affect longer-term outlook
key_facts.excerpt: SEMI chief executive Ajit Manocha told Reuters that risks arising from geopolitical tensions were unlikely to curtail the boom this year, though persistent shortages of raw materials may affect the longer-term outlook.

key_facts.fact: Omdia raised its 2026 semiconductor market forecast to $1.35 trillion (up 62.7% YoY), a 32-percentage-point revision from its January forecast, driven by memory chip price surge
key_facts.excerpt: Market research firm Omdia projected that global semiconductor market revenue will reach approximately $1.35 trillion this year, up 62.7% year-over-year. This represents a sharp 32-percentage-point increase from the 30.7% growth forecast Omdia issued in January.

key_facts.fact: Helium prices rose sharply in March after the US-Israel war on Iran disrupted natural gas processing in Qatar; South Korean chipmakers warned of potential bromine shortages
key_facts.excerpt: Prices of helium, a by-product of natural gas processing, rose sharply in March after the U.S.-Israel war on Iran disrupted such operations in Qatar, the world's largest supplier of liquefied natural gas (LNG). South Korean chipmakers have also warned of potential shortages of bromine.

sources.title: Global Semiconductor Sales Increase 25% from Q4 2025 to Q1 2026
Global trade group SEMI sees robust demand for chips despite geopolitical risks
Global Semiconductor Market Nears $1.4 Trillion as Memory Supercycle Drives 32-Point Surge in Outlook

stories.headline: Palantir Q1 Revenue Up 85% to $1.63B, Fastest Growth Since IPO; Raises FY26 Guidance to 71% Growth

key_facts.fact: Palantir reported Q1 revenue of $1.63 billion, up 85% YoY, beating analyst estimates of $1.54 billion — the fastest growth since its 2020 direct listing
key_facts.excerpt: Palantir's revenue grew about 85% in the quarter, marking the fastest increase in sales since at least 2020, the year the company went public through a direct listing.

key_facts.fact: Adjusted EPS was $0.33 vs $0.28 expected; GAAP net income quadrupled to $870.5 million with a 53% net income margin
key_facts.excerpt: Earnings per share: 33 cents adjusted vs. 28 cents expected. Net income roughly quadrupled to $870.5 million, or 34 cents per share.

key_facts.fact: US revenue grew 104% YoY to $1.28 billion; US government revenue up 84% to $687 million; US commercial revenue up 133% to $595 million
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. revenue grew 104% year-over-year and 19% quarter-over-quarter to $1.282 billion. U.S. commercial revenue grew 133% year-over-year to $595 million. U.S. government revenue grew 84% year-over-year to $687 million.

key_facts.fact: Palantir raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $7.65-$7.66 billion (71% YoY growth), well above consensus of $7.27 billion and prior guidance of ~$7.19 billion
key_facts.excerpt: We are raising our revenue guidance to between $7.650 - $7.662 billion... representing a growth rate of 71% Y/Y.

key_facts.fact: CEO Alex Karp said Rule of 40 score reached 145% and predicted the US business would double again in 2027; revenue per employee hit $1.5 million annualized
key_facts.excerpt: 'Our financial results now demonstrate a level of strength that dwarfs the performance of essentially every software company in history at this scale,' Palantir CEO Alex Karp wrote. Revenue per employee reached $1.5 million on an annual basis.

key_facts.fact: Palantir closed 206 deals of $1M+, 47 deals of $10M+, and total contract value of $2.41 billion, up 61% year-over-year
key_facts.excerpt: Closed 206 deals of at least $1 million, 72 deals of at least $5 million, and 47 deals of at least $10 million. Closed total contract value of $2.41 billion, up 61% year-over-year.

sources.title: Palantir Reports Q1 2026 U.S. Revenue Growth of 104% Y/Y and Revenue Growth of 85% Y/Y

stories.headline: FDA Approves Auvelity as First Non-Antipsychotic Treatment for Alzheimer's-Related Agitation

key_facts.fact: FDA approved Auvelity (dextromethorphan-bupropion) for treatment of agitation associated with Alzheimer's disease, making it the only FDA-approved non-antipsychotic for this indication
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved a new first-in-class treatment, Auvelity (dextromethorphan-bupropion), for the treatment of agitation associated with Alzheimer's disease. Auvelity is now the only FDA-approved treatment for Alzheimer's-related agitation that is not classified as an antipsychotic.

key_facts.fact: Auvelity works by modulating NMDA and sigma-1 receptors, a different mechanism from antipsychotic medications; it was already FDA-approved for major depressive disorder
key_facts.excerpt: Auvelity is designed to ease agitation by modulating the activity of two brain cell receptors called the NMDA and sigma-1 receptors. The therapy was already FDA-approved to treat adults with major depressive disorder.

key_facts.fact: Agitation affects roughly three-quarters of Alzheimer's patients and can include restless pacing to physically or verbally lashing out at others
key_facts.excerpt: Agitation — which can include everything from restless pacing to physically or verbally lashing out at other people — is a common Alzheimer's symptom, reported in roughly three-quarters of people with the disease.

key_facts.fact: Approval based on four Phase 3 studies (ACCORD, ACCORD-2, ADVANCE-1, ADVANCE-2) plus a long-term extension study; patients on placebo were more likely to relapse
key_facts.excerpt: Axsome's application was based on data from a battery of clinical trials including four Phase 3 studies called ACCORD, ACCORD-2, ADVANCE-1, and ADVANCE-2... patients who switched to a placebo were more likely to experience recurring agitation than those who kept taking the active therapy.

key_facts.fact: Auvelity was the only FDA-approved product to show statistically significantly longer time to relapse of agitation symptoms vs placebo in a long-term study
key_facts.excerpt: 'Auvelity is the only FDA-approved product to result in a statistically significantly longer time to relapse of agitation symptoms, compared to placebo, in a long-term study,' George Grossberg, MD, professor at Saint Louis University School of Medicine, noted.

sources.title: FDA approves Auvelity to treat Alzheimer's-related agitation

stories.headline: Panthalassa Raises $140M Led by Peter Thiel to Power Floating Data Centers With Ocean Waves

key_facts.fact: Panthalassa raised $140M led by Peter Thiel at a $1B valuation to develop floating data centers powered by ocean wave energy
key_facts.excerpt: Panthalassa, which aims to power floating data centers using energy generated by ocean waves, raised $140M led by Peter Thiel, source says at a $1B valuation.

key_facts.fact: The company aims to harness untapped ocean energy resources thousands of miles from human settlements to power AI infrastructure
key_facts.excerpt: The oceans are an incredible untapped resource for energy that can power AI. The most intense wave energy is thousands of miles from human settlements.

key_facts.fact: VSC Ventures also participated in the round; the company was described as one of their 'coolest investments'
key_facts.excerpt: You're not supposed to publicly pick favorites as an investor, so I'll just say this is one of our *coolest* investments @VSCVentures

sources.title: Panthalassa raises $140M for ocean wave-powered floating data centers
